speaker: The Chairman
text: Second Supplementary Estimates of Expenditure for the financial year 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2021, contained in Paper Cmd 28 of 2020.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I shall deal first with the Heads of Expenditure in respect of which amendments stand on the Order Paper Supplement.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Low-income transnational families have been particularly hard-hit by COVID-19 and circuit breaker measures.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Close to half were not earning any income from work because their jobs did not allow them to work from home.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Migrant spouses are particularly vulnerable in times of economic crisis as they are often the first to be let go, especially since COVID-19 related job support schemes do not provide incentives for employers to retain non-citizen workers.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Ministry consider funding an online platform to facilitate job-matching for these workers at a national level so that employers looking to hire overseas workers could be encouraged to hire from this pool, which includes migrant spouses, first?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: According to AWARE's survey, more than half of the respondents reported that, in addition to their current household income, which mostly falls below $2,000, they still need more than $300 a month to meet their basic needs.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: To cope, some have cut down on food-related expenses; a few said they were unable to pay rent.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Government consider relaxing the citizenship criteria for COVID-19 related financial assistance and make them available for all migrant spouses with a Singaporean in their household?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Only when we include those who have chosen to make Singapore home and help raise our children can we truly say we are “SG United”.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, if I may now address Ms Ong’s questions on support for transnational families and migrant spouses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The support schemes announced at the various Budgets aim to provide support to Singaporean households, including those with non-citizen members, who may be concerned over household expenses during this period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include household-based benefits like GST Voucher – U-Save rebates and Service and Conservancy Charges Rebate under the Care and Support Package, and the Solidarity Utilities Credit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This was explained by the Deputy Prime Minister during the round-up of the Solidarity Budget and in response to a Parliamentary Question from Mr Murali Pillai last month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If they or their Singaporean family need further financial support during this challenging period, they may seek help through the MSF Social Service Offices (SSOs), which provide assistance to those who fall into financial hardship.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MSF has exercised more flexibility when considering ComCare applications during this period, to ensure affected Singaporean families, including those with non-citizen members, can get help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SSOs will also work closely with other agencies and partners to address the family’s needs, including employment concerns.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There are also many Social Service Agencies and those in the community providing support to families in need.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These include Social Service Agencies funded by MSF to support transnational families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Migrant spouses who are allowed to work can access work opportunities through many channels, including job advertisements, referrals, recruitment agencies and various online platforms.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would Ms Anthea Ong like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head O of the Estimates be reduced by $100.” As Singapore extends safe distancing measures to protect lives, we must remain aware of how doing so leads to not only “costs” for our economy and businesses, but real and significant detriments to our mental health.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: A similar picture of a “mental health pandemic” is being observed in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Caregivers Alliance Limited (CAL) has shared with me that their caseloads have significantly increased in the last three months, with many care-givers reporting increases in mental health relapses and crisis incidents experienced by their care recipients, four of them have even lost their loved ones to suicide just in the last six weeks.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: To deal with the psychological fallout from COVID-19, countries like New Zealand and Scotland have relied heavily on mental health experts in their COVID-19 response.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The extended safe distancing measures for Phase One of exiting the circuit breaker is likely to prolong mental distress, as we continue to deal with social isolation, the lack of personal space, and disruption to routines.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Would the Ministry consider appointing mental health experts for the Multi-Ministry COVID-19 Task Force, to advise on mental health implications as we extend the stringent safe distancing measures to re-open cautiously?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: As the resident unemployment rate climbed to a 10-year high of 3.3% in March, a survey by Profile Asia indicated that many employees are facing increased levels of stress dealing with uncertainty over future pay cuts and their jobs.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng talked about seeking out “opportunities in adversity” during his Fortitude Budget Statement.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The COVID-19 crisis also offers us an unprecedented opportunity in equipping businesses and workers for the rebound through improving workplace wellness.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: A recent report has linked business recovery from COVID-19 to a sustained focus on employee well-being.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Would the Ministry consider appointing at least one mental health expert on the Emerging Stronger Task Force to advise on well-being policy interventions to strengthen our recovery from this crisis?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The mental health of our nation is important, and the Government is committed to taking care of the mental well-being of Singaporeans, especially during this COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The pandemic has resulted in increased stressors that impact our mental well-being, given the changes in daily routines, social isolation and economic uncertainty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, more support needs to be put in place to address the mental stress that the COVID-19 pandemic and circuit breaker measures have brought about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Multi-Ministry Task Force (MTF) recognises this and has been tapping on mental health professionals from MSF, MOH and MOE to give inputs on the psychological aspects of COVID, and in the enhancement and development of mental health initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our public healthcare institutions (PHIs) continued to provide essential mental health services during the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Some of our community mental health partners continued to conduct urgent home visits for vulnerable clients and those at risk of self-harm, harm to others, or at-risk of deterioration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Tele-consultations were also adopted by PHIs and community service providers so that they remain connected with their clients to ensure their mental health needs are supported.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For employees, MOM, along with other agencies, such as MSF, AIC and NCSS, issued an Inter-Agency Advisory with practical steps to support employees’ mental well-being and provided counselling resources for employers and workers to tap on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For students, school counsellors continue to support those in need through face-to-face and online sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Vulnerable students were actively identified for further support and invited to return to school during the CB period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOE also provided students with Holiday Care Packs containing resources and helplines on mental well-being and cyber wellness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As we gradually ease movement restrictions, we have also paid special attention to addressing the well-being of seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The decision to allow children to visit their parents or grandparents is one example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Emerging Stronger Task Force (EST) was set up primarily to develop recommendations on how Singapore should refresh, reimagine or reset its economic strategies, to stay economically resilient and build new sources of dynamism in the post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, besides the two co-chairs, the remaining members are industry representatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nonetheless, the EST has committed to consult multiple stakeholders to draw on insights beyond its membership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOH, together with the relevant partners and agencies, will continue to ensure that mental health support and services are accessible to persons in need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will take into consideration the impact of COVID-19 on mental health as we undertake a whole-of-Government review of our mental health strategy and study ways to further strengthen our community mental health services to support new vulnerable groups that may emerge due to COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Could I then ask if MOH has the intention to increase funding for these community health organisations?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Many of them have actually shared with me that, well, we know that there is a long tail to the mental health impact and they are also sharing that increased funding would really help them in terms of increasing their capacity.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I have no doubt that even as we undertake a whole-of-Government review of our mental health strategies to strengthen mental health services, where there is a need to access additional funding, that could be put into the next Budget, if necessary.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would Ms Ong like to withdraw the amendment, please?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head V of the Estimates be reduced by $100."  I would like to declare my interest as an impact investor and also founder of social enterprise Hush TeaBar and A Good Space Co-operative.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I appreciate that this is a longer term view to maintain our attractiveness and robustness as one of the top start-up eco-systems in the world.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: However, start-ups are inherently risky and identification of "promising start-ups" is often a hit-and-miss endeavour.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I know this as an investor and an entrepreneur.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Economic downturns often sift the wheat from the chaff, leaving the most resilient ones behind.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: By intervening in the sifting process, is there a danger of the Government artificially propping up ailing start-ups and distorting market forces?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Moreover, an inability to adapt to the changing economic landscape by continuing to rely on Government financing seems to go against the spirit of start-ups.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: What was the reason behind dedicating $285 million to support "promising start-ups", which can also tap into the many support schemes for SMEs, over other areas of spending, such as extending greater support to struggling households like public rental waivers?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Which immediate concerns or areas of national priority will the $285 million be used to address, for example, climate change?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: What are the checks and balances in place to ensure that the $285 million will be effectively utilised?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, start-ups play an important role in our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Anthea Ong asked why our start-ups need more help and how we intend to identify the promising ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, the answer is in her question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Start-ups, especially those that work on cutting-edge technologies, need to be nurtured with long-term patient capital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: COVID-19, unfortunately, has sharply curtailed the availability of such capital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Other countries like the UK and France have introduced similar measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Without help from the Government, many high potential start-ups will likely scale back their innovation activities or even cease prematurely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: That will be a loss to Singapore and will certainly have a detrimental impact on Singapore's innovation eco-system, which we have painstakingly built up over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: By helping promising start-ups sustain their growth momentum, we want to maintain the vibrancy of our eco-system and maximise the value of our innovation-related investments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To impose market discipline, the scheme will operate on a co-investment basis with private sector investors that have expertise in assessing the value and viability of start-ups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will also help crowd in more private capital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These co-investors can also offer industry insights, networks and even mentorships to help our start-ups to succeed better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic presents many immediate challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But even as we address the immediate ones, we must not forget to put in place plans for our future, so that Singapore, our companies and Singaporeans can emerge stronger post-COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Start-ups are a critical part of these plans.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I am very happy to hear that we will be co-investing in these start-ups.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Could I ask the Senior Minister of State if there is a plan in this co-investing to take equity or is that in the form of grants?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: And if, once the start-ups are on their way to growth, would we then ask for a clawback of the initial investment or grant?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for the question.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: A convertible bond is of one of the most expedient instruments to invest into a company in this current COVID-19 situation as discussions on equity valuation can be deferred to the next funding round, hopefully, when the economic situation is better.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would Ms Ong like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head S of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, many Singaporean workers who have lost income due to COVID-19 have benefited from the Government's income support schemes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These help schemes are differentiated between employees, who are eligible for the COVID-19 Support Grant, and the self-employed, who are eligible for the Self-employed Person Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This difference in benefits has caused some concern among workers who believe that their employment classification – as an employee or as a self-employed person – does not accurately reflect how they work, their control over their income, and their COVID-19 income risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: There are also workers who are not sure which group they belong to.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: They are paid on a piece rate per course.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The Universities were informed this treatment was incorrect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, the Universities switched to using contracts of service, which made them employees.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But the adjuncts are actually still paid on a per-course basis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: They still lack the income security of full-time or even part-time employees, although they now do get CPF contributions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Another example is that of workers who are unsure of their status.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I was told that a hair stylist needed to apply for a COVID-19 income support grant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Is the hair stylist an employee or self-employed?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It turns out that this person operates under a reverse commission model.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The stylist works in a hair salon, she pays the salon owner a percentage of the revenue she brings in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But then, the salon owner may believe that the stylist works for them and may impose conditions on how and when they work.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These cases often have no formal contract or they have a contract which is poorly drafted.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: An appeal was made demonstrating self-employment and I believe the stylist got their SIRS payment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But the point is that these work arrangements are not always easy to classify sometimes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Can we do more to ensure that help is calibrated to the workers' actual income risks and income level, rather than their classification status?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: For example, if a part-time or contract employee faces substantial income risks, because they are hired on a case-by-case basis, could they be considered for SIRS benefits instead?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: We should also review the legal status of different work arrangements.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Other countries are exploring an intermediate classification between employment and self-employment for gig-economy workers and those whose work is under the partial control of another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, really, to cope with the severe shocks induced by COVID-19, we should aim for benefits tailored to income risks, rather than tailored to the classification of the worker.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Anthea Ong, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Hence, establishing workplace adjustments for mental health must be an urgent priority for business and overall economic recovery.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The inter-agency advisory for employers to support employee well-being, which Senior Minister of State Amy Khor alluded to earlier, is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Protecting jobs is as important as protecting employability, which includes mental well-being.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Can the Ministry integrate the inter-agency advisory into the Job Support Scheme (JSS) such that beneficiary employers must demonstrate effort to introduce workplace adjustments to support their employees?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I propose that businesses should adopt Employee Assistance Programmes (EAPs), mental health insurance coverage for employees and/or other well-being programmes to qualify for JSS payouts in July and October.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Also, will the Ministry consider encouraging these progressive well-being practices with further incentives?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I propose that the Ministry expands the scope of the Enhanced Work-Life Grant beyond flexible working arrangements (FWAs), for funding EAPs and/or other well-being programmes.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The Government has signalled that the COVID-19 Support Grant is an important—sorry, that is the wrong one.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The intention behind the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) to protect jobs and salary is welcome.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: It appears that workers have been threatened with dismissal if they complain about their employer's errant behaviour.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I applaud this strong stand against abuse of the scheme.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: However, I also note that IRAS continues to encourage individuals to report malpractices and abuses of JSS.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Despite IRAS' promise that whistle-blowers' identities will be kept strictly confidential, I foresee many cases in which this will pose little obstacles to the employer discovering the identity of the whistle-blower.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Some complaints may never make it to the authorities because the employees do not know of the avenues for complaint or are afraid of souring their relationships with their employers.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: This is particularly true for elderly or lower income employees who will be most affected by the loss of their jobs and are consequently more vulnerable to exploitation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, as we go through these challenging times, the Government is committed to protecting livelihoods and sustaining businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The support provided through the Unity, Resilience, Solidarity and Fortitude Budgets is targeted to help keep businesses viable and workers employed, so that they can tide over this crisis and recover quickly as the economy restarts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM, with the support of the four Budgets, seeks to achieve this in three ways, namely: one, ensuring fair support for all workers – both for the employees and self-employed persons (SEPs); two, championing fair employment practices; and three, promoting mental well-being in our workplaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) has cushioned the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak on the labour market by helping employers to hold on to their employees and continue paying their salaries, even during the Circuit Breaker period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We introduced the SEP Income Relief Scheme (SIRS) to help Singaporean SEPs with less means and family support tide over this difficult period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Although SIRS is means-tested, the Government has taken into consideration that these are unprecedented times.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For comparison, usually, about 50,000 SEPs receive Workfare each year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In other words, they are assessed to need more help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We understand that many SEPs may have seen their incomes fall.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In other words, one would have to be in the top 20% taxpayers' bracket to exceed the SIRS criterion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As for the Annual Value (AV) of property criterion, it serves as a proxy for wealth and family support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government has similarly sought to cover more people under SIRS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We understand that some of the SEPs who exceed the AV criterion may not themselves own these higher-end properties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Rest assured they can still appeal to be considered for SIRS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will work with NTUC to assess the circumstances on a case-by-case basis and ensure that the scheme helps SEPs who most need it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Even if an appellant is not eligible for SIRS, we will certainly connect him or her with other relevant agencies like the Social Service Offices (SSOs) to offer other forms of assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, in administering schemes and programmes, such as SIRS, the Government has always partnered various like-minded organisations to better serve Singaporeans and our businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is a key feature of tripartism and has served our Singaporean workers very well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, we work with the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF), NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) and Singapore Manufacturing Federation (SMF) to administer the Work-Life Grant (WLG).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Likewise, the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) is our appointed programme manager for SGUnited Traineeships, working with host companies to review and approve the scope and development plans of the proposed traineeships.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Other Government agencies, such as Enterprise Singapore (ESG), have also partnered with Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) to administer schemes for companies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In governing these schemes, the responsible Ministries and agencies determine the policy parameters, including the eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Ministries set clear boundaries within which our partners must operate, and any exceptions would require the Ministry’s approval.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, over the past few years, several Members of Parliament and members of the public have raised concern that some employees could be misclassified as SEPs and, as a result, not received CPF contributions from their employers and other employee benefits, such as leave entitlement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira also raised this question earlier in his cut.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In determining whether an individual is an employee or SEP, the Singapore Courts consider factors, such as the degree of control exerted by the company and its ability to decide on the hours of work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, given the wide variety of work arrangements today, each case must be evaluated based on the specific circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government applies a similar approach to the Courts when assessing the employment status of an individual.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To ensure that the employees are not misclassified as SEPs and denied their statutory employment benefits, MOM follows up on complaints – every one of them that we received – and ensures that the employers make rectifications where needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, arising from feedback from adjunct teaching associates a few years ago, MOM worked with our Autonomous Universities to ensure that the CPF contributions and leave entitlements were provided to those working as employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I understand that during the circuit breaker period, adjunct teaching associates have continued to receive full salaries from their Universities which are supported by the JSS payouts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government has provided substantial support through the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS) to help our employers retain and pay local workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We take a whole-of-Government approach to identify such fraudulent cases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As highlighted in the media release by IRAS on Wednesday this week, there are severe penalties for any attempt to abuse the JSS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure Ms Ong that workers need not be afraid to come forward to report any infringement of employment laws, because the Employment Act protects them from wrongful dismissal by employers, especially those who seek to punish workers for exercising their rights.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM takes all feedback on employment law infringements very seriously.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During this difficult period, workers and employers have to work even more closely together than ever before and strive to maintain open channels of communication.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As Mr Louis Ng pointed out, employees may need greater work flexibility to deal with the disruptions that arise due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Likewise, Mr Desmond Choo and Ms Sylvia Lim raised points regarding the challenges of workers, in particular, women, face and how Flexible Work Arrangements (FWAs) can benefit employers, employees and the society in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: FWAs help workers better prepare and better balance their commitments at home and at work, and enable women to remain in the workforce, gain work experience, earn higher wages and assume leadership positions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM has been working with the tripartite partners to improve workers' access to FWAs, such as by providing support via the Work Life Grant (WLG) and recognising progressive employers through the Tripartite Standard on FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As a result of COVID-19, many more companies are working from home now and are benefiting from FWAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will seize the opportunity to continue this momentum and ensure that work-from-home arrangements are sustained beyond the COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will not only strengthen business resilience; it will better support work-life harmony for all workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As more businesses gradually resume operations, workers will take some time to adjust to the new normal as well as different working arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since the start of COVID-19, there has been many changes and adjustments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We understand that workers may face additional stress, and some may have mental health challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Ms Anthea Ong that we must look into our workers' mental health as we also seek to protect as many jobs as possible during this challenging period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Ong had suggested that we consider introducing additional requirements to qualify for JSS payouts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, the intent of JSS is, as I have mentioned earlier, to help the companies retain and pay for local workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is to help as many companies stay afloat and keep jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, really, the JSS is a temporary scheme designed to help companies save jobs for Singaporeans during this period of economic uncertainty.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Adding too many conditions would only make it more difficult for the employers to benefit from JSS or, inadvertently, cause a delay in employers getting the urgent help they need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Jobs may be lost if the employers do not get timely help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Instead, we have been working on other ways to encourage our employers to implement progressive practices and workplace adjustments to take care of our workers' mental health needs in the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are also working closely with the various Government agencies and the Labour Movement to provide our employers with resources that can support their workers' mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, what I have just shared are ways in which we are supporting our workers and employers to overcome the challenges arising from COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During the circuit breaker, we have all come across many heart-warming and heartening stories of how businesses, workers and Singaporeans are rallying behind one another as one community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we slowly reopen the economy and transit to a new normal, I am confident that the unity and the fortitude of our workers and the employers will see us through this crisis and help us emerge stronger together.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low for her response.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Should there be a mechanism to make companies that are unaffected by or even profiting from the crisis return their JSS payouts?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: How are we actually making sure that this is made known, particularly to the more vulnerable employees, that they have this right?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Many of them are sharing with me that they are so afraid to come forward because, first of all, they do not know they have this right and, secondly, they are worried about employers actually making life harder for them.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The longer the question, the shorter the answer.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I will just keep it to two then, Mr Chairman, on your cue.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member, Ms Anthea Ong, for her supplementary question.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On the first one about whether there are companies profiteering from the crisis.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier on, I mentioned that the JSS is targeted to help companies retain and pay their local workers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In designing the JSS, MOF as well as MOM and the various Ministries sought to achieve a balance between targeted assistance and also administrative efficiency, because this is really a crisis period.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: You want to make sure that the help reach the intended target audience as expeditiously as possible and make sure that we save every job.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is really important to provide the support to them.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, to identify and exclude individual employers from this scheme will certainly need another level or, in fact, a few levels of administrative operations to sift through, especially when the eventual economic impact to them remains uncertain.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It may not be administratively efficient to do so.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I just want to share the balance between providing the help in an efficient way to the target audience vis-a-vis operational complexity.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Now, I also want to reassure Ms Ong —

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we really urge the workers to report such errant employers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member will be familiar with our various programmes like Work Right and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We do have MOM officers going out not just to big companies, but also to small ones to share with them the rights of our workers, what are their rights under the Employment Act and how they would be protected.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, they need not fear because the Employment Act protects them, especially those who have been wrongfully dismissed.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Would Ms Ong like to withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Chairman, it is myself who is withdrawing the amendment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Chairman, I wish to thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for her kind replies.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Head I, Ministry of Social and Family Development.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: However, I would like to bring attention to several aspects of the scheme that obstruct it from fully meeting the needs of those who need it most.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Applicants have to first show that they have lost or will lose income over three months.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For those whose initial conditions of no pay leave or reduced income do not reflect at least three months, they will have to wait to become eligible for CSG.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This will be the case for most employees, especially lower wage workers, many of whom who do not even have a document from their employers spelling out conditions of leave.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: It would be inconceivable to expect employers who lay off employees to provide a confirmation that the employee will have three months of income lost, nor is it logical to expect individuals to show loss of future income of at least three months now.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: From May 2020, there is no interim support scheme that can help to tide such individuals over.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Further, the amount and duration of support provided under CSG is ungenerous, especially when compared to the Self-employed Persons Income Relief Scheme (SIRS).

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The duration of support should also be extended from three months to nine months or when applicants are able to secure a job, whichever is earlier.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: If the Ministry disagrees, individuals who have been financially affected by COVID-19 will be forced to apply for ComCare financial assistance in the interim or after they have exhausted their full CSG payout.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Given the almost five-fold difference in income eligibility criteria of CSG versus ComCare, will the Ministry consider enhancements to ComCare such as: (a) increasing the income eligibility caps for ComCare and (b) increasing the flexibility with regard to supporting documents required?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: For instance, instead of strictly requiring bank statements, one could be allowed to produce documents that show job or income loss.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: While MSF provides support for affected employees through CSG, employees are also supported through the Jobs Support Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Self-employed persons (SEPs) are mainly supported through the Self-employed Persons Income Relief Scheme or SIRS.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Employees who have lost their jobs can apply for CSG immediately without waiting for three months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Employees who are placed on involuntary NPL or experiencing reduced monthly salary need not wait till they are affected for three consecutive months to apply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They are eligible for CSG if their NPL or salary loss has already started and they provide supporting documents, such as a letter from their employer, showing that the involuntary NPL or salary reduction will be for at least three consecutive months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The "three or more consecutive months" requirement for involuntary NPL and salary loss scenarios is to ensure that help is channelled to those who have greater needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Daily-rated and ad hoc workers may qualify for CSG if they meet the eligibility criteria.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Workers who do not have employment contracts due to the nature of their work may approach their nearest Social Service Offices or SSOs to make a self declaration on their employment status.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SSOs will undertake further checks against applicants' past CPF records and facilitate their CSG application if they qualify.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Individuals eligible for CSG and without bank accounts can approach SSOs for assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Those who are ineligible for CSG and are in financial need can apply for ComCare, which provides financial assistance for basic living expenses and other support such as household bill expenses and medical expenses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For those with urgent financial needs, SSOs, grassroots organisations and Family Service Centres can provide them with ComCare Interim Assistance.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, please wrap up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are not hard thresholds and each case is considered on its own merit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Supporting documents including bank statements and payslips enable SSOs to accurately assess the applicants' circumstances, savings and needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SSOs exercise flexibility as needed to provide the necessary financial assistance and social support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SSOs can conduct their interviews and assessments electronically and applicants can submit their supporting documents via email.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Ong, would you like to withdraw the amendment, please?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I shall now deal with the remaining heads of expenditure in respect of which no amendment stands on the Order Paper Supplement.

speaker: The Chairman
text: In respect of the Second Supplementary Main Estimates, they are Heads K, Q, T, U, X and Z.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I propose to take those Heads of Expenditure en bloc.

speaker: The Chairman
text: In the respect of the Second Supplementary Development Estimates, it is Head T.
